Generate meta cells via MetaCells2 (divide and conquer)

rs_metacells2.Rd

Rust port of the metacells divide and conquer pipeline. Works on the raw counts directly, so no embedding or kNN graph is needed. Cells are split into piles, each pile gets its own feature selection, similarity graph and partition, and outliers are re-run in further rounds. Cells sharing a rare gene module are piled together first unless switched off in dac_params.

Usage

rs_metacells2(
  f_path,
  cells_to_keep,
  mc2_params,
  dac_params,
  target_size,
  seed,
  verbose
)

Arguments

f_path

String. Path to the counts_cells.bin file.

cells_to_keep

Integer vector. 0-indexed positions in the count file of the cells to include.

mc2_params

List. The per-pile parameters, see params_sc_metacells2().

dac_params

List. The divide and conquer parameters, see params_sc_metacells2_dac().

target_size

Numeric. Library size to normalise the aggregated counts to.

seed

Integer. For reproducibility.

verbose

Boolean. Controls verbosity.

Value

A list with the following elements

  • assignments - The meta cell assignments in the original cell space.

  • aggregated - The aggregated raw and normalised counts in CSR form.

  • dissolved - Logical per included cell. Was the cell's candidate dissolved in its last pile.

  • level - Integer per included cell. Outlier round that placed it.

  • rare_module_of_cell - Integer per included cell. 0-indexed rare gene module, -1 for none.

  • rare_module_of_gene - Integer per gene. 0-indexed rare gene module, -1 for none.

  • selected_genes - Integer. 1-indexed genes selected in any pile plus the rare module genes.

References

Ben-Kiki, et al., Genome Biol., 2022.
